claim_en: THE OFFICE IS SERVICE BEFORE ME, ENTERED BY OFFERING. le-khahano-li ('to serve Me as priest') rendered le-shammasha KODAMAI ('to SERVE BEFORE ME') five times across the chapter — the priest-verb decoded as audience-service; and the installation idiom u-mileta et yadam ('fill their hand,' 28:41) rendered u-tekarev yat KURBANHON ('OFFER THEIR OFFERING') — office entered by sacrament.

source: Onkelos on Exod 28:2 + 28:40; the census row at Mishnah Yoma 7:5
claim_en: THE GARMENTS' DECLARED PURPOSE AND THE EIGHT-COUNT. li-kar ul-tushbechan ('for HONOR and for SPLENDOR') — stated for Aaron and repeated for the sons; the case shelf's census rides: the high priest serves in EIGHT garments, the common priest in FOUR (Mishnah Yoma 7:5, this exam's docket) — the chapter's six-list plus the plate and the pants.

THE JUDGMENT ORGAN. choshen mishpat rendered the breastplate of DINA ('JUDGMENT') — Aaron BEARS THE JUDGMENT of the sons of Israel on his heart before the LORD TEDIRA ('continually'), with the Urim and Tummim INSIDE it, and the names as remembrance on shoulders and heart: a portable query interface worn on the body — pairing EX25-05's fixed answer address at the ark-cover.

source: Onkelos on Exod 28:28 + 28:32; the lash rows at Babylonian Talmud Yoma 72a
claim_en: TWO STANDING PROHIBITIONS IN THE VESTMENTS. ve-la yitparek ('the breastplate shall NOT BE DETACHED from the ephod') and la yitbeza ('the robe's opening shall NOT BE TORN') — the poles-never-removed class (EX25-04) extended to the garments; the case shelf counts both among the lash rows (Babylonian Talmud Yoma 72a).

THE ANNOUNCED ENTRY. Bells of gold alternating pomegranates on the hem — ve-yishtama kalei ('its SOUND SHALL BE HEARD') entering the sanctuary and leaving — ve-la yemut ('that he not DIE'): an audible-entry protocol with a death sanction; the garment announces its wearer.

source: Onkelos on Exod 28:36-38; the acceptance row at Mishnah Zevachim 8:12
claim_en: THE WRITTEN PLATE AND THE ACCEPTANCE FUNCTION. The gold plate engraved KETAV MEFARASH ('in CLEAR SCRIPT'): Holy to the LORD — writing enters the vestments in the chain's own explicit-script vocabulary (the same formula as the signet-engraved stones, 28:11 + 28:21); and Aaron BEARS THE INIQUITY of the sacred offerings — TEDIRA — le-raava ('for ACCEPTANCE'): the plate propitiates offering-defects (Mishnah Zevachim 8:12, this exam's docket).

WEAR OR DIE, FOREVER. The linen pants complete the set; worn on entry or approach — ve-la yekablun chova vimutun ('that they not bear guilt and DIE') — KEYAM ALAM ('an EVERLASTING STATUTE') for him and his descendants: the garments as a condition of service under the perpetuity token.

THE MIRROR TABLE. Ezekiel 16's care-list mapped item for item onto the tabernacle's institutions — washed/laver, anointed/oil, CLOTHED/THE GARMENTS, tachash-shod/the covers, linen/the priestly linen, silk/the cloud-answering curtains, crown/the ark-cover, rained bread/the showbread, went-before-them/the lamp — under the rule DO FOR ME AS I DID FOR YOU: every institution answers a recorded act of care.

The Urim and Tummim are consulted only IN the eight garments, and only for the KING, the COURT, or one whom the COMMUNITY needs (Mishnah Yoma 7:5) — the portable judgment organ of EX28-03 carries an authorization layer: full uniform and a qualified petitioner, or no query. Seated from the Step 9 Tetzaveh exam, auto-seat law.

No fewer than three treasurers and seven trustees, never fewer than two officers over public funds (Mishnah Shekalim 5:2) — anchored at this verse's own plural take-verb: and THEY shall take the gold. Seated from the Step 9 Tetzaveh exam, auto-seat law.

The acceptance function is scoped: the plate propitiates the IMPURE and does not propitiate the TAKEN-OUT (Mishnah Zevachim 8:12) — EX28-06's bearing-the-iniquity clause given its case-shelf boundary. Seated from the Step 9 Tetzaveh exam, auto-seat law.

source: Mishnah Pirkei Avot 5:6 + Babylonian Talmud Sotah 48b (Step 9 Tetzaveh exam)
claim_en: The stones set in their FULLNESS — whole, uncut — were written by the SHAMIR of the twilight census (Mishnah Pirkei Avot 5:6, the census held at EX16-15; the bridge Babylonian Talmud Sotah 48b assigns it here). Seated from the Step 9 Tetzaveh exam, auto-seat law.

THE FRONTPLATE'S STATE MACHINE. Broken — all agree it does not accept (Abaye's frame); hanging on a peg — the dispute runs on the verse's own two clauses: R. Yehuda's on-the-forehead-and-he-shall-BEAR (contact required) against R. Shimon's tamid-la-ratzon (always ACCEPTING — the always-word moved from the wearing to the function, with the Yom Kippur linen proof). The scope: all hold public impurity pushed aside and needing the plate — except R. Yehuda's lone permitted-outright arm (EX28-11's scoped propitiation at its sugya). Not an ordeal: for-acceptance-and-not-for-calamity, with Rav Ashi's for-THEM gate. And the export: the plate's tamid teaches the tefillin's every-hour touching, a-fortiori from its single Name. Filed F-103, auto-seated (round 27, the vestments block).

THE VESTMENTS' FORM FILE. The shoulder stones' six-and-six quoted at the verse, the second stone by-their-birth (Judah advanced on the first), fifty letters at twenty-five per stone. Woven, not needle-work — with the sleeve exception. The tefillin slot: the hair showed between plate and turban — the vestment set leaves the tefillin their place (two seats). The sounding ring on this day's pan answering the sound-shall-be-heard clause where the robe is absent. And the jurisdiction: priest and service garments at the GREAT altar only. Filed F-104, auto-seated (round 27, the vestments block).

source: Onkelos Exod 28:1-4, 28:11, 28:15, 28:21, 28:28-38, 28:40-43; Midrash Tanchuma, Tetzaveh 1; Yoma 71b:6-14, 72a:1-9, 72b:3, 7b:4-5, 44b:16, 5b:4; Zevachim 88b:2-8, 26a:21, 95a:4, 119b:18; Arakhin 16a:13-16; Sanhedrin 83b:13-14; Sotah 36a:12, 9b:22; Bava Batra 8b:9; Megillah 12a:7, 12b:10; Shabbat 31a:7, 12a:4; Gittin 20b:1; Makkot 22a:8; Menachot 25a:2, 11a:5, 42b:13; Chullin 138a:6; Yevamot 60b:13; Mishnah Yoma 1:1, 3:4, 3:7, 7:1, 7:3-5; Zevachim 2:1, 8:12; Horayot 3:4-5; Megillah 1:9; Sotah 9:12; Sanhedrin 2:1; Tamid 5:3; Shekalim 5:1-2; Middot 1:4; Kelim 1:9; Shabbat 6:9
claim_en: THE SPEC GRADED AGAINST ITS OWN RUN — THE RUN'S ADDED TOKENS ARE THE SPEC'S PARAMETERS, EIGHT FROM SIX PLUS TWO, THE GOLD-BEARING FOUR. Exod 28 in cold_run_vestments.py (196 of 196) graded as a scene against Exod 39: the list of 28:4 names six, the plate and breeches make eight; the gold-bearing blocks are Yoma 7:5's added four; Yoma 71b-72a's thread counts run on the run's tokens (five 'fine linen' at 39:27-28, the added 'twined' at 39:24, the process verse 39:3) — M-22's third form, the parameter, on a homograph ('fine linen' = 'six'); 'and Aaron shall bear' at four seats; 'before the LORD' five to none; the two bans with the particle test; the stone-names' homographs and Ezekiel's nine; the breeches answering the altar's nakedness clause by call; the many-garmented by call; the atonement table by adjacency. Nine effects.
